newsitem.title: GERMANY: Scientologists at world book fair in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Scientologists at world book fair in Germany.

text.p: The Church of Scientology, accusing the German government of conducting a witch hunt against it, set up shop on Wednesday outside the world's biggest book fair.
"It is important for us to be here for the sake of freedom of speech," said church spokeswoman Ute Mydla-Fischer.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling Christian Democrats have urged anti-extremist watchdog agencies to keep a close eye on Scientology, which has 30,000 adherents in Germany.
Family and Youth Affairs Minister Claudia Nolte has accused it of indoctrinating youth and masquerading as a church while being driven largely by economic motives.
The party's youth wing called for a cinema boycott of the film "Mission Impossible" because its star Tom Cruise is a member of the church.
The dispute over the sect has strained relations between Bonn and Washington, with U.S. State Department officials urging Germans to defy the boycott and see the film.

"Mission Impossible has been the number one film in Germany. That speaks for itself," said Mydla-Fischer as Scientologists put their books on display in a bright yellow double-decker bus outside the 110-nation book fair.
"There has been a witch hunt against us. There is a constitution in Germany and we have rights like every other religion," she said.

The religion, founded in 1954 by the late American science fiction novelist L. Ron Hubbard, claims more than eight million adherents worldwide. High-profile members include Cruise's wife Nicole Kidman and another big Hollywood star, John Travolta.
Followers are recruited largely through personality tests and then sold books and courses of treatment to resolve problems diagnosed in the tests.
Mydla-Fischer, speaking in a bus bedecked with Hubbard's books, said: "It is important to read them so people can make up their own minds. There is nothing to be afraid of."
German officials resent attempts to liken their treatment of Scientologists to Nazi Germany's slaughter of six million Jews in the Holocaust.
Church of Scientology President Reverend Heber Jentzsch refuses to back off.

"The parallels to the Nazi era drawn by those who are familiar with its pogroms are the result of modern-day violations by the government and party officials which carry the same hallmarks," he told the weekly news magazine Der Spiegel in a recent interview.
